RFC9136-3.1-1.note: Re-judged 2026-10-02 (BGP c31 judge). RFC 9136 Section 3.1: "The Length field of the BGP EVPN NLRI for an EVPN IP Prefix route MUST be either 34 (if IPv4 addresses are carried) or 58 (if IPv6 addresses are carried)." Send: evpn rfc9136_length_test.go::TestRFC9136IPPrefixRouteSentWithLength34Or58 (EncodeNLRIHex type5, IPv4 with and without label -> 05 22 + 34 octets, IPv6 -> 05 3A + 58) and ::TestRFC9136IPPrefixRouteNeverSentWithAnotherLength (two labels refused, nothing encoded). Receive: ::TestRFC9136IPPrefixRouteReceivedWithAnotherLengthIsRefused (Length 33/35/57/59 -> ErrorIs ErrEVPNInvalidAddress) beside the HEAD 34/58 decode positives. The InProcessRouteEncoder path (encode.go EncodeRoute) builds type 5 with exactly one label and shares (*EVPNType5).WriteTo, so the same Length holds there by construction; it is not driven by these units. Judge overlay: the parse guard reduced to `len(data) < 34` turns only the receive negative red. Records on buildEVPNFromParams (+/-) and parseEVPNType5 (-).

RFC9136-3.1-3.note: Single-polarity positive (row marker). (a) forbidden: decoding the RD or the Ethernet Tag ID at other than the RFC 7432 layout (8-octet RD, 4-octet tag after the 10-octet ESI); (b) TestEVPNType5IPv4 assert.Equal("0:65000:100", evpn.RD().String()) and assert.Equal(uint32(10), evpn.EthernetTag()) go red on a misplaced or misdecoded field. Only a type-0 RD is driven; RD type decoding is the shared ParseRouteDistinguisher.

RFC9136-3.1-4.note: Re-judged 2026-10-19 (independent auditor, after 4283f8d2e3). Verdict stands: enforced. RFC 9136 Section 3.1: "The Ethernet Segment Identifier MUST be a non-zero 10-octet identifier if the ESI is used as an Overlay Index (see the definition of "Overlay Index" in Section 3.2).  It MUST be all bytes zero otherwise." No producer change since 0411b53e91 (git log over internal/component/bgp/plugins/nlri/evpn and update_text_evpn.go shows only 4283f8d2e3, which touches internal/le/interoplab/bgp/check_extras.go alone). checkOverlayIndex is unchanged and still the only gate before newEVPNType5, whose two non-test callers (plugin.go buildEVPNFromParams, encode.go l2vpnRouteToEVPNParams) both call it first. Tagged units pass at HEAD (go test -run 'TestRFC9136Overlay|EVPNType5ESIGateway' over nlri/evpn and cmd/update, ok). Interop, closing the prior note's owed item: 4283f8d2e3 makes bgp-evpn-gobgp originate through update text ('... ip-prefix rd 1:1 esi 00:01:02:03:04:05:06:07:08:09 etag 0 prefix 10.77.0.0/24 overlay-index esi label 0', internal/le/interoplab/bgp/helper.go:202, path parseEVPNSection -> buildEVPNFromParams -> checkOverlayIndex) and wait for GoBGP's JSON NLRI to read "esi":"ESI_ARBITRARY | 01:02:03:04:05:06:07:08:09","etag":0,"prefix":"10.77.0.0/24","gateway":"0.0.0.0". bgp-evpn-frr now only asserts FRR keyed the route [5]:[0]:[24]:[10.77.0.0] (FRR 10.3.1 prints no type-5 ESI), so FRR proves acceptance, not the octets. Both scenarios reported 1 passed in the commit body; not re-run by this judge. Red recorded in the commit body: a GOFLAGS overlay passing ESI{} to newEVPNType5 in buildEVPNFromParams made bgp-evpn-gobgp fail its assertion 3 (GoBGP read esi single-homed), so the interop discriminates the non-zero-when-index clause at a second implementation. The zero-otherwise clause and every refusal remain unit-proven only (TestRFC9136OverlayIndexESIRefusedOtherwise, four mutants each red on its own subtest per the 2026-10-18 note); an interop peer cannot observe a route Ze refuses to send, so no interop negative is owed. The interop check is untagged reach/goal evidence and adds no tag; it carries no discrimination record of its own under ./le rfc discriminate-record, only the commit-body red.

RFC9136-3.1-5.note: (a) forbidden: accepting an IP Prefix Length above 128; (b) TestEVPNType5PrefixLengthTooLong/ipv6 require.ErrorIs(err, ErrEVPNInvalidPrefix) on length 129 goes red if parseEVPNType5 accepts it; positive TestEVPNType5IPv6 decodes 64. The send side cannot exceed 128 (netip.Prefix). The ipv4 subtest's tag (33 > 32) proves the non-normative 'can be set to a value between 0 and 32' sentence, not this MUST NOT: a misplaced tag, listed as a finding.

RFC9136-3.1-6.note: Re-judged 2026-10-19 (independent auditor, after 4283f8d2e3). Verdict stands: enforced. RFC 9136 Section 3.1: "The GW IP Address field is a 4- or 16-octet field (IPv4 or IPv6) and will encode a valid IP address as an Overlay Index for the IP prefixes.  The GW IP field MUST be all bytes zero if it is not used as an Overlay Index." No producer change since 0411b53e91 (git log over internal/component/bgp/plugins/nlri/evpn and update_text_evpn.go shows only 4283f8d2e3, which touches internal/le/interoplab/bgp/check_extras.go alone). checkOverlayIndex is unchanged and still the only gate before newEVPNType5, whose two non-test callers (plugin.go buildEVPNFromParams, encode.go l2vpnRouteToEVPNParams) both call it first. Tagged units pass at HEAD (go test -run 'TestRFC9136Overlay|EVPNType5ESIGateway' over nlri/evpn and cmd/update, ok). Interop, closing the prior note's owed item: 4283f8d2e3 makes bgp-evpn-gobgp originate through update text ('... ip-prefix rd 1:1 esi 00:01:02:03:04:05:06:07:08:09 etag 0 prefix 10.77.0.0/24 overlay-index esi label 0', internal/le/interoplab/bgp/helper.go:202, path parseEVPNSection -> buildEVPNFromParams -> checkOverlayIndex) and wait for GoBGP's JSON NLRI to read "esi":"ESI_ARBITRARY | 01:02:03:04:05:06:07:08:09","etag":0,"prefix":"10.77.0.0/24","gateway":"0.0.0.0". bgp-evpn-frr now only asserts FRR keyed the route [5]:[0]:[24]:[10.77.0.0] (FRR 10.3.1 prints no type-5 ESI), so FRR proves acceptance, not the octets. Both scenarios reported 1 passed in the commit body; not re-run by this judge. The GoBGP needle includes "gateway":"0.0.0.0", so GoBGP reads an all-zero IPv4 GW IP under overlay-index esi: positive interop evidence for this MUST. The recorded red broke the ESI only; no red was forced on the gateway (for example passing a non-zero gateway past checkOverlayIndex), so the interop's discrimination of the GW IP clause is unproven and the needle's gateway half is a positive-only observation. That does not lower the verdict, which rests on the unit proof: TestRFC9136OverlayIndexESINonZeroOnlyAsIndex pins GW 00000000 under none and esi, TestRFC9136OverlayIndexESIRefusedOtherwise refuses gateway 10.1.2.1 under esi, none and no keyword, three mutants red on their own subtests (2026-10-18 note).
